Today's meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the proceedings of today's meeting of the National Assembly commence. (13:20 hrs) Honourable members, names have been received to speak during Zero Hour. I will now provide time for the members to speak.
First, Honourable Member Gita Devkota.
Honourable Gita Devkota (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, (13:21 hrs) It is said that imports are regular for management, but there is a shortage of gas in the country, or the government's stove is not burning. Citizens from Bhaktapur to Bharatpur are queuing for hours. Holding babies in their laps and empty cylinders in their hands, they have to endure sun and rain. Honourable Chairperson, why is there a shortage of gas only in the kitchens of the public? Why is there no shortage in the kitchens of the government and ministers? How did this situation arise? Why did it arise? Until when will this continue? The government should be accountable. Gas should be immediately provided to citizens through every dealer. The transparent distribution system, black market control, and adequate storage and pipeline control should be expedited. Speeches on good governance do not suit when the public's stoves are extinguished, government. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Chandra Bahadur KC.
(13:22 hrs)
Honourable Chandra Bahadur KC (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, (13:22 hrs) a few days ago, the statements made by Rastriya Swatantra Party MP Khagendra Sunuwar against the Inspector General of Police Dan Bahadur Karki in the meeting of the Public Accounts Committee were seriously objectionable, and I express my sorrow over them. I urge through the Honourable Chairperson that the Rastriya Swatantra Party take this seriously and proceed with action in this regard. Along with this, I want to say again, the Prime Minister's statement regarding the border should be removed from the parliamentary record as soon as possible. The government's stove is not burning, the stove needs to be lit. Saying this, I request leave here. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhala.
(13:23 hrs)
Honourable Meenasingh Rakhala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Chairperson, (13:23 hrs) due to the continuous rainfall since Shrawan 28th, there has been unimaginable loss of life and property in various parts of the country. In Rolpa's Thawang Rural Municipality-5, 11 houses were buried in a severe landslide, and 13 citizens are missing. So far, the bodies of 4 people have been recovered. I offer my heartfelt condolences to the mother of former central member of CPN UML, Naveen Roca Magar, and all those who lost their lives in the landslide. I extend deep sympathy to the bereaved families and wish for the speedy recovery of the injured. The news of 4 deaths and 7 injuries in the landslide in Jajarkot's Bheri Municipality-2 Risad has also stunned the mind. These incidents are not just natural disasters; they are also a test of disaster preparedness, rescue, and the state's immediate presence. Due to continuous rainfall, floods, landslides, and mud have affected BP Highway, Kanti Lokpath, Dolpa Road, and other major roads. (....Time Expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Ranjit Karna.
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Ranjit Karna (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, (13:24 hrs) I say with great pain today, my family could not cook today due to the gas shortage. It has been stated from the government itself that if the electricity is used too much, the transformer will explode. Now, how will the public cook? Gas is scarce, electricity induction transformers explode, if one goes to find firewood, they get caught by the Forest Act if they enter the jungle, so what is the alternative? There is no gas, don't use electricity, don't cut firewood. Whichever monk comes, his ears are pierced. Honourable Chairperson, this pain is not mine alone, but that of millions of Nepalis. It has been 4-5 days since this house held the government accountable, and there has been no hearing so far. I urge that the problem of gas be resolved today at all costs. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri.
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Ram Kumari Jhankri (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Chairperson, (13:25 hrs) I remember the days 11 months ago. Some friends who dared to lead on the ruins of the earthquake, on the bodies of the police, took leadership. Elections were held, peaceful elections were held. The Home Minister and the police chiefs are making such defamatory remarks in society by levelling unnecessary accusations. What is this social media, media, phone tapping? Where is society heading? Is society without questions in such a society? Where are they trying to take society? If anyone holds a public office, will everyone gang up to tear them down? Will that person not be allowed to live in society with dignity? What is this society? Therefore, I used to question the government, question within my party, and question myself. But today, I will question this society because it is a dynamic society, a living society, and this society is not without questions. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Roshni Meche.
(13:26 hrs)
Honourable Roshni Meche (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Chairperson, (13:27 hrs) the issue of gas has been raised a lot because it is a basic necessity for all our citizens. Even during the dark night of the blockade, the then Oli government provided alternatives to the citizens when there was a gas shortage, and no one's stove was allowed to go out. But today, even with a majority government, the public is forced to stand in line for hours to cook gas due to a lack of cooking gas. When will the easy supply of this gas be ensured? The government must answer in the house. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Basudev Ghimire.
(13:27 hrs)
Honourable Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, (13:27 hrs) I offer condolences to those who have died in Rolpa, Jajarkot, and other districts due to the continuous rainfall in the past few days, and I urge the government through the Honourable Chairperson to arrange free medical treatment for those injured in the floods and landslides. Similarly, I urge the Nepal government to arrange relief for the displaced families. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the order of speaking during Zero Hour concludes here. (13:28 hrs) Honourable members, names have been received on a party basis to speak during Special Time. I will now provide time for the Honourable members to speak. First, Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra, time 25 minutes.
Honourable Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, (13:29 hrs) I have prepared to speak for a long time today. Honourable Chairperson, it is difficult. If someone asks what is the biggest achievement of this government, my answer will be only propaganda. If someone asks where the failure of this government lies, then failure lies only in results. The government wants only propaganda and does not want results. The government must give results, not hope, to the people. The main achievement of a government that does not deliver results is only propaganda. Therefore, the current government is running on a propaganda campaign rather than for the people. The government has identified propaganda instead of the people's needs and their solutions. The people's demand is good governance, employment, and development.
Honourable Chairperson, the government seems eager to create an atmosphere of its own propaganda rather than working to win the people's trust. The government is trying to enjoy the festival of announcements. The people want to see the results of work, not announcements. The government should go to the villages and talk to the farmers. If they get fertilizer on time, they say they can double production. Talk to the youth waiting in line for foreign employment. They say that if they get a job in Nepal for even 20-24 thousand, they wouldn't leave their homes for the heat of the Gulf in their youth. Ask the people with gloomy faces waiting in line at the hospital; they want to prolong their lives by taking loans at high interest from moneylenders. Visit the shops of small businessmen; they have their own complaints. Farmers who produce vegetables say they are selling vegetables cheaply as if giving them away for free, but the price of the same vegetables reaches the sky by the time the customer buys them. Where is the loot? Where is the fault? The government should find this out. This government came to power by spreading rays of hope among the people. But slowly, the seedlings of despair are beginning to sprout. The claim that we are development-oriented will only be meaningful when development is reflected not only in speeches or talks but also in the state system, in the citizen's experience, in their demeanor, and in their movements. But that is not visible anywhere. The light is not shining.
In a book titled 'Lippu-Likhit', a Singaporean historian Kishore Mahbubani writes that from 1 to 1820 AD, i.e., from 2057 BS to 1870 BS, the two largest economies in the world were China and India. Only then did Europe start to make progress. Along with India and China, Nepal was also a relatively prosperous country, it would not be an exaggeration to say. History testifies that in ancient times, India, from the sea to the Himalayas and from the Indus to Afghanistan, was a prosperous region. However, in the last 3 centuries, especially after the East India Company entered India, Nepal alone seems to have fallen behind in the race for prosperity compared to the average. Now, I want to add one thing: the main and first task of this government, which the people have given a huge mandate to, beyond the imagination of this constitution, is to find out the main reasons why the country has not achieved the prosperity that the people and leaders have thought of in 37 years of democracy, and to find solutions to those reasons. But even before completing 5 months in government, it seems there is no time to even think about or debate and discuss that.

What shall we talk about and what shall we not, Nepal and South Korea had the same economic condition until the 1950s. But today we are scrambling to become their servants. If I don't talk about neighboring India, my statement will be incomplete. A few years ago, at a conference of excellent entrepreneurs, the then Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said, "Today India's annual production will increase by 9 percent, tomorrow by 10, the day after by 11. This is not just our dream. Know that, establish multinational companies, open banks, make Hollywood, capture foreign media, the Indian government is ready to provide all necessary help." Think about how much the chests of entrepreneurs must have swelled with such a speech. India, our neighbor, to whom we sold food grains just 35-40 years ago. The same land, the same country, today we buy food grains from them. Now, think about it, they are dreaming of becoming masters of the world, and we cannot even get jobs as servants in the least developed countries. What a tragedy for Nepal? How will the country progress?

Perhaps because the old parties could not do what they promised, the public has given the National Independent Party a two-thirds majority and elected them. We all had the hope that the country would surely progress now, but just as the morning gives an indication of what the day will be like, this government seems to have chosen its path like Surdarji choosing an elephant. It seems unable to determine whether it is the tail, the ear, or the trunk for building the country. Is the government hesitant in assuring the private sector? Consider how foreign investors will be attracted. Let's see if there is something other than the country's strength that hinders the pace of Nepal's development? The government may have succeeded in publicizing itself on various social media, but no concrete plans or programs seem to have been put forward to improve the living standards of the people. I have some questions. What is the concrete plan to create employment in the country? What progress has been made to ensure timely supply of fertilizer, seeds, and market for farmers? What plans are being made to complete projects on time by spending capital expenditure on time? Where is good governance visible in practice amidst the talk of good governance? What plans are being made to improve the living standards of the citizens of Sudurpashchim, Karnali, and Madhesh? I want to add a question. We do not want to see the government fail, but the parliament has the right to evaluate whether the government is working according to the people's expectations. The height of any government is measured not by its publicity, but by the people's trust. Yes, the tenure of power can be determined by the constitution and law, but the tenure of political trust is determined by the people. A government should not get angry from criticism, but should learn from it. Let me say one thing, Kabir Dasji said, "Keep your critics close, build them a hut in your courtyard," meaning, keep those who criticize you close, build them a house in your own courtyard so that you know what your mistakes are. Therefore, criticism is a good aspect for the government.

I want to give one suggestion to the government: it may take time to form a government, develop, and change traditions, but it may not take even a moment for the people's minds to change. Therefore, the government should work to preserve the people's trust, because once trust is gained, no excessive majority can shake it. The government should not consider the people's patience as its success, nor should it consider the people's silence as its popularity. In a democracy, elections may take 4 years, but if the people decide to make a decision in their minds, it can happen in a very short time. We do not want instability, we want to see development, we want to see good governance in practice, we want to see government accountability. But not by bypassing parliament. Again, I say the government has an excessive majority, but a majority cannot change the truth, and a majority can suppress questions, but it can never suppress the voice and mind of the people. A majority, the applause of the majority, can make the parliament resound, but historically, respect has only been earned through work, and trust is also earned through work. There are examples worldwide of some movements that have uplifted countries and established peace, but there are also examples of some movements that have pushed countries into civil war.

I say again, the government has the pride of a huge majority, but has the people's equally huge trust been maintained? Yes, the government has power, as well as means and resources, but have the means and resources reduced the people's cost of living? Have they eliminated unemployment? They have despair and worry about the future. Therefore, it is not important how much power the government has, but what change that power has brought to the lives of the people. Today the government recites a long list of achievements. We ask, how many people got employment from that list, how many industries were opened, how much did the farmers' income increase, was the supply of chemical fertilizer easier than in previous years, or did they face more difficulties? This year, an unprecedented event occurred where one had to go to jail for trying to smuggle two sacks of fertilizer into Nepal. It was said that government services would be easier, how easy have they become? How much effort is required to get an industry license? Is the government's report card the answer to the resolution of such public problems? May the government have the wisdom to engage in protecting the mandate given by the people, this is my prayer.

Today, those in the government who used to give speeches in villages saying, "We will no longer have to shed sweat in the Gulf for employment," are being mocked by the line of youth at the airport going abroad. This scene is not normal. A generation is forced to leave the country. There are no youth in our villages, only a procession of elderly mothers and fathers. There are fields, but no laborers. Barren land mocks us. The number of students in schools, especially colleges, is decreasing. Should we consider economic success solely by counting the remittances sent by our youth, or should we focus on the development of industries and factories without selling the electricity produced in the country? In Nepal, when discussing agriculture, it is always seen as a priority on paper. But the government's reach does not seem to extend to the farmers' fields. Stock is shown in fertilizer warehouses, but there is a crisis when needed. Not only fertilizer, but also seeds and irrigation are in short supply. Moreover, after production, they do not get a market and a fair price for the market. Without ensuring even this, they talk of an agricultural revolution! Farmers produce, middlemen earn, but consumers are forced to buy at high prices. How long will this cycle continue?

Government, we are in the opposition. Our job is not to remain silent about the government's mistakes. We ask questions because the public demands answers from us. We provide warnings because the constitution has given us that responsibility. We criticize because if criticism is prohibited in a democracy, democracy itself weakens. Those who govern in a democracy must accept criticism and learn from it. We want the government to succeed because the government's success is the people's aspiration. For the government to succeed, it must have the courage to listen to criticism, the courage to correct mistakes, and the courage to answer the people's questions.

Finally, this is the only thing I say at the end. Power comes and goes, governments are formed and fall, ministers come and go, but the people remain here, the country remains here, and history also remains here. Give youth opportunities, not assurances; give farmers fertilizer and markets, not slogans; and give businessmen an environment for investment, not fear. Let's make Sudurpashchim a place of development, not assurances, and let's make parliament a place to save the people, not to save power. This is democracy, this is respect for the people.

I will say a few more things, there is still time. From 2007 BS until today, the bell of instability has always rung in the country. Democracy came in 2007 BS, the people were happy. But in 2017 BS, not only was the constitution strangled, but elected Prime Minister Vishweshwar Prasad and other leaders were imprisoned. There was a continuous desire to run the Panchayat system. In protest against that absolute Panchayat system, after the student movement in 2036 BS, the king was forced to announce, "Do you want multi-party or partyless?" The partyless system was victorious, not because I won, but because in my village, only five people voted for the Village Development Committee. That didn't work either. In 2046 BS, when Marichman's government was about to end, the king became restless. Realizing it wouldn't work, the king appointed Lokendra Bahadur Chand as Prime Minister. But Lokendra Bahadur Chand's prime ministership lasted only three days. After that, on Chaitra 26, the king was forced to announce multi-party.

Even after the movement of 2046 BS, the country, we said, has made the best constitution. It was propagated that such a constitution does not exist in the world. But there were many protests. Friends who have returned from the roots are among us. Such a commotion happened in the country. Wow, the republic came. We thought the country would soar after the republic came. We thought the country would progress. Even after the republic, are some conspiracies being hatched again? What is happening? After bringing a system like a republic, the highest system should be considered. Not only that, the Madhesh movement had also added federalism to it. Such a beautiful system in Nepal, and now we are ready to play games with it? I don't know what it is. We only see the results, we don't see the schemes woven ahead. We only saw it on the 23rd-24th, we don't know what schemes were hatched before that and what resulted from them.

Therefore, it is the duty of all of us to protect this constitution, this excellent constitution, in the coming days. Therefore, I want to make a request that everyone's attention be directed towards protecting that constitution.

Now I will say one more thing.

"Shuro'si krutavidgho'si darshaniyo'si putrak. Yasmin kule tvamutpatno gajastra na hanyate॥"

Meaning, the cubs were hungry, the tigress went in search of prey. After searching all day without finding prey, she found a fox cub wandering. Bringing the fox cub, the cubs said, "Mother, he looks like our elder brother. We will raise him, not eat him," and they kept him with them. They grew up together, growing bigger. One day, a herd of elephants was coming along the same path. The fox cub ran here and there, saying, "Hey brother, wake up, wake up, wake up, the elephants are coming, the elephants are coming." The cubs were playing. The mother tigress returned from the jungle. The fox cub went ahead and said to the tigress, "Mother, mother, today the elephants almost trampled us to death. I told them to run, run brother, run, I ran here, I ran there, they were just sleeping." Then the tigress came forward and spoke to her cubs, "What is it?" The cubs said, "Yes, elephants came this way. The elephants looked at us, but did not come towards us. If they had dared to come towards us, we would have torn off their trunks. We would have..." Hearing this, the tigress said, "Oh, if my children follow this brother's words, my children may become cowards tomorrow. It's very difficult. So she told him, "You may be brave, you may be very clever, very wise, you may be handsome, son. But in the family you were born into, elephants are not killed." I do not want to elaborate on this.

Now, the government is riding a tiger. If it gets off that tiger, the tiger will eat it. If it tries to control that tiger, if it tries to move that tiger forward, it cannot run like a horse. It is constantly thinking about how to eat this prey.

I am only worried if it happens. The government that rode a tiger's horse, one, I will tell you about a farmer. A farmer planted a pumpkin in the field. Another pumpkin grew on its own nearby. As we watched, the pumpkin vine grew so big in the monsoon that it climbed onto a grafted mango tree, not only climbing it, but also fruiting a large pumpkin and almost breaking the mango branch. Oh, the mango tree was scared, and other plants in the field started getting scared. But before the monsoon ended, by the time the month of Ashwin arrived, the pumpkin vines withered away. Therefore, plants that grow fast have a short lifespan, please be aware of this and let's proceed slowly towards developing the country with patience. Now, there are 22 seconds left, the Prime Minister must be responsible to the parliament. You were elected Prime Minister by that parliament, if you are not responsible to that parliament, it won't work. Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire, time 10 minutes. (13:55 hrs) After this, Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal. Honorable Shri Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, on August 12, 2024 (Shrawan 27, 2081 BS), dozens of people lost their lives in a landslide in Ward No. 5 of Thabaad Rural Municipality, many are missing, and some are injured. Hearing about this tragic incident has caused us immense pain, and our desire is that such incidents and natural disasters do not occur in this country. But after such incidents and hearing about such suffering, we are hearing that the government, by providing necessary resources and means to the local government, could have provided relief to the affected victims and saved their lives in time. We are hearing that the people affected by the earthquake have not received any relief yet. Hearing about the current incidents, from the perspective of disaster management and the Home Minister, the Home Minister went to that place and was involved in rescue efforts; this work was done by the government, according to the news. I hear in the news that he went to Gorkha and talked about drinking water. People are drinking water by collecting it in buckets these days. When there is a crisis, we should be there, the government should provide guardianship when people are in trouble. The government's attention has not reached here. This has greatly affected people's lives and livelihoods. We are hearing about a gas shortage, which is unimaginable. Even if we bring firewood from the furniture, the landlord won't allow us to burn it. We can't even light a fire, so gas is essential here. Let's look at the lives of every person, every student. They have to rent a place, go to study at 10 or 9 o'clock, how long will the children wait in line, when will they fetch water, when will they get gas, the market is so expensive. How can they buy and eat? At such a time of extreme impact, fruits are also expensive, vegetables are also expensive, oil and rice are also expensive. We have not heard any monitoring from the government, nor have we heard the government speak about providing relief to the people today. When we brought democracy and a republic, we thought that by mobilizing the youth, including women and all castes and ethnicities, this country would become beautiful and we would fulfill all our needs. But today, even when the youth are in the government, we hear and see that people's lives are further affected, which is a sad thing. We have not been able to build the country as we envisioned, and we ourselves are saddened by this. Therefore, in a parliamentary system, the parliament elects the Prime Minister, the Prime Minister is accountable to the parliament, and the Prime Minister is the guardian of the country. Today, the Nepali people are proud and hopeful that the country has a Prime Minister who is technologically adept. However, we have heard in the House of Representatives and are seeing in the National Assembly that the Prime Minister has not come to parliament to answer, address the Nepali people, and fulfill the responsibility of a guardian. This causes us immense sadness, and the Nepali people must also be sad. Therefore, the government must be accountable, the Prime Minister must be accountable. Yesterday, on this very floor, the Home Minister said, 'I worked hard for seven months.' He mentioned that he was very tired from working hard for seven months. If you are tired, you have a majority, so you can take turns. Why do you have to complain so much here? If you are tired, you should take turns. If the load you are carrying is heavy, you rest, and after a while, when the fatigue is gone, you carry it again. Therefore, I think it would be appropriate to arrange such turns. Another thing, yesterday, a school-going child sent money via e-Sewa to buy a mobile phone. I went to the Cyber Bureau and inquired, and many people were there. I was told that someone taught him to fill out the KYC, and he went and did that work, and all the money in his bank was emptied, leaving him with zero. He is there filing a complaint at the Cyber Bureau. We are talking about using technology, but those who are learning are falling into trouble. Who will say this? People like us who know how to use a mobile phone a little, who know how to send a little, had their money looted, even the money of the sister studying in college, and the money of the mother sitting at home. Her money was looted in the name of filling out the KYC. Her bank had 6.5 lakh rupees, which became zero. Such anarchy, such smuggling, such fraud is rampant in this country today. Why has this become rampant? Is it because those who commit such misdeeds are let go? Or is there a way to control it? What is the government's plan? A clear answer is needed, and a mother sitting at home, thousands of mothers, can become destitute, their wealth is looted, and their lives can also be unsafe. Therefore, the government must be serious and pay attention to this, and the government must move forward with a plan to control this fraud. Through you, Mr. Speaker, I want to draw the government's attention, and I request that we, the Nepali people, should hear about the government's plan. Finally, I want to speak about the plan for 2082/083 BS. In the red book for 2082/083 BS, many plans were included, and the Nepali people hoped that development would happen in their areas. The government formed with the support of the Janjiti movement did not implement those plans, stopped them, and many planned works for 2082/083 BS could not be carried out. It is now time to survey the plans for 2083/084 BS. The Nepali people are wondering what plans the current government, the youth's government, the two-thirds government, the stable government will bring. There is an atmosphere of uncertainty regarding the plans. From the government's side, we do not see any plans for change in the lives of youth, women, children, and farmers. We do not see continuity either; there is continuity of some old plans. There is not a single new plan from this new government. If we do not start any new work, will our country, our villages, not fall behind in development? If we were unable to work in the last fiscal year and are unable to move forward with work this year, then our development and construction works will also fall behind, the lives of the Nepali people will be affected, and this government will not be able to provide concrete plans to the Nepali people. Therefore, the government must lead in all these fundamental matters, the government must answer, and it must be such that the Nepali people feel that there is a government in Nepal, that the Prime Minister of Nepal is on the side of the Nepali people. The government might think that working together in a team of two or four people, eight or ten people, one hundred or fifty people, will result in good work. But if King Birendra's palace at Narayanhiti could not be secured, how safe can we be with the work done by a few people? This is obvious. Therefore, I draw your attention and wish that the government focus on sustainable development in a way that the Nepali people can feel it. Finally, Nawalparasi West, Susta is submerged due to the flooding of the Narayani River. I want to conclude my remarks by drawing the government's attention to the rescue of the people affected by the flood. Thank you. (14:01 hrs) Presiding: Honorable Vice-Chairperson Ms. Lila Kumari Bhandari. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal, time 15 minutes. (14:05 hrs) After this, Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar. Honorable Shri Prem Prasad Dahal (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, today I am going to speak. For the past three decades or 35 years, 37 years, efforts are being made to construct a narrative that nothing has happened and to spread disinformation about it. Is this the reality? Is today's Nepal the same as it was 30-35 years ago? In this period, I have tried to discuss some fundamental issues with indicators of what the country has achieved and what it has not. First of all, Honorable Chairperson, (1) Economic Growth: Since 2047 BS (1990 AD), the average economic growth has been between 3 to 4 percent. In the last two decades, the average economic growth has been around 4 percent. During this period, especially in the fiscal years 2073/074 and 2074/075 BS, during the post-earthquake period, the government led by KP Oli achieved an economic growth rate of 8.6% in 2073/074 BS and 7.4% in 2074/075 BS, and then a continuous economic growth rate of 7% thereafter. At that time, Nepal was successful in being among the top 10 countries achieving high economic growth, which was a matter of pride for us. Gross Domestic Product: In 2047 BS (1990 AD), it was 1 kharba 20 arba (120 billion NPR), and it has now reached 66 kharba (6.6 trillion NPR). The per capita income in 2047 BS (1990 AD) was 185 US dollars, while it has now reached 1535 US dollars; this has certainly happened. What was the annual budget? The annual budget for 2047/048 BS was 23.45 arba (23.45 billion NPR), and it is now 21 kharba 24 arba 34 crore (21.2434 trillion NPR); this has also happened. Poverty Alleviation: Regarding poverty alleviation, the World Bank published a report a year ago stating that Nepal has made a leap. The World Bank defines extreme poverty as an income of less than 2.15 US dollars per person per day. Looking at this, extreme poverty, which was 55 percent in 2047 BS (1990 AD), has sharply decreased to 0.37 percent; this is a World Bank report. Has this happened or not? In 2052 BS (1995 AD), absolute poverty was an average of 42 percent, and it has now come down to 20.27 percent. Multidimensional poverty is 27.4 percent, and the Gini coefficient based on consumption is 0.30. I will provide more information regarding poverty later. (3) Inequality in income and consumption is decreasing. The share of the lower and middle classes in national income is increasing. In 2052 BS (1995 AD), the income of the bottom 10 percent of the population in poverty was such that the income of the rich, the top 10 percent of the rich, was 21 times higher, while now it has decreased to 6 times. Similarly, Physical Infrastructure: In 2047 BS (1990 AD), 8,328 kilometers of roads were built. Now, 1,40,000 kilometers of roads have been built. The length of the roads has increased by approximately 12 times.

The condition is that it has been met. Road access has reached the headquarters of all districts and most rural municipalities. New technology is being used in the construction of tunnels and high bridges. Wooden bridges and zip lines appear to have been almost displaced. Some internal work on the Kathmandu-Nijgadh Expressway is being completed. Infrastructure has also expanded in the field of sports. For example, the Kirtipur Cricket Ground was built with floodlights and a pavilion within a year. Efforts are underway to achieve it in higher education as well, this must have happened too. More than 3.6 million beneficiaries are receiving social security allowances. 2.84 million workers are registered in the contribution-based social security fund. In 2048 BS, 1 percent of families used tractors, while now, according to agricultural data from 2078 BS, it is 40 percent. The area has increased from 3 percent to 28 percent. How much paddy is produced now? Services: Tourism, transportation, communication, and other service sectors have expanded. The communication sector has truly made strides. Television channels, FM radio, online news, and newspapers are expanding widely. If we talk about non-governmental organizations alone, there were 220 in 2047 BS, while now there are 50,000. This has provided significant support for socio-economic development. Housing: Families living in houses with कच्ची (kaccha - unpaved/mud) roofs have decreased from 90 percent to 20 percent. When it reaches 0.45, it is considered to be in a medium state of human development. Nepal's progress is significant compared to South Asia, from the perspective of the Human Development Index. Nepal has moved from a country with low human development to medium human development. All these achievements are due to improvements in education, increased access to health services, and increased personal income, leading to significant progress in the Human Development Index. Presiding Officer: Respected Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal. (14:44 hrs) Chairperson: Honorable members, the special time for speaking has now concluded. (14:49 hrs) Honorable members, the question-and-answer session with ministries will now commence. Honorable members, after the honorable minister responds, the questioning honorable member, if they wish, may ask a supplementary question related to their original question within one minute. Honorable members, I would like to invite the honorable Minister of Youth, Labor, and Employment, Mr. Ramji Yadav, to the rostrum to answer the questions posed by the honorable member. Honorable members, I now provide time to the questioning honorable member, Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota, to ask her question. Honorable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Through the esteemed Chairperson, I have a question for the honorable Minister of Youth, Labor, and Employment. Due to the lack of sufficient employment opportunities within the country, hundreds of youths are forced to go abroad for employment daily. Incidents of death, fraud, abandonment, and exploitation of Nepali citizens abroad are continuously increasing. What concrete steps have been taken in coordination with the Ministry of Home Affairs and other ministries to stop youth migration, create employment opportunities within the country, and make foreign employment safe and dignified? Thank you. Chairperson: Honorable Minister. (14:51 hrs) Honorable Minister of Youth, Labor, and Employment, Mr. Ramji Yadav: Thank you. Esteemed Chairperson, first of all, I would like to thank the honorable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota for raising serious questions regarding youth migration and employment. This issue is indeed serious. Therefore, the government fully agrees with the concerns raised by the honorable member. However, I ponder how these concerns arise. Why did such concerns not arise for 35 years? If concerns were indeed raised, why were concrete steps not taken? If concrete steps had been taken earlier, perhaps this situation would not exist today. Perhaps a foundation would have been laid, and people could have come and worked. Unfortunately, today we are working negatively on employment. But this does not mean we have the luxury of delay; there is absolutely no such luxury. Our priority is clear: to create sufficient employment, self-employment, and income opportunities within Nepal, making youth feel that there are possibilities for building their future and working in their own country. With this objective, the government is currently working differently to create employment. When I joined this ministry, the ministry's focus and work were more on foreign employment than on domestic employment. But now we have made a paradigm shift. Embracing the responsibility of creating employment, we have placed it as a high priority for the ministry. For instance, we have taken policy and legal steps to stop youth migration and create employment within the country. Firstly, regarding the legal and policy framework, we are in the process of formulating a new employment policy and have advanced the necessary process for theoretical agreement to enact the National Employment Promotion Act. We are setting policy bases for the selection and management of employment generation programs at the local level. Furthermore, by creating the 'Integrated Service Delivery Procedure for Employment, Skills, and Entrepreneurship, 2083', arrangements have been made to operate these three subjects in an integrated manner. In this way, a mandatory and incentive-based policy is being adopted towards making 390 hours of training mandatory for quality skill development. We also want to present the progress report so far. The Employment Skills and Entrepreneurship Centers in all 753 local levels across the country have been established and are being operated as the main structure for providing employment. Based on the demand from industrialists and entrepreneurs, extensive discussions, coordination, and cooperation are ongoing with private sector industrialists, entrepreneurs, and non-governmental organizations for workplace-based training. To address the changing demands of the labor market, approximately a dozen programs, including the concepts of the care economy and digital employment, have been launched since the beginning of the current fiscal year in coordination and cooperation with various government ministries and bodies, and work is underway. Under the programs of the current fiscal year, skill and employment fairs are going to be organized in all seven provinces. The National Employment Promotion Program is being focused on increasing agricultural productivity as a national campaign to substitute agricultural imports. A system for profiling the skills of individuals returning from foreign employment is being developed using information technology, and skill testing through Recognition of Prior Learning is being given high priority, with efforts to connect their skills and capital to domestic production and entrepreneurship. Furthermore, the data of the unemployed is being managed through the Employment Management Information System (EMIS), and the technical development and upgrading of the Labor Communication System are being carried out to connect employers and workers. The Government of Nepal has declared the 'Decade of Domestic Employment Promotion' and is advancing a long-term campaign to expand employment opportunities within the country, reduce unemployment, and decrease dependence on foreign employment. An concept for operating programs in 12 different sectors where employment opportunities exist in Nepal has been developed, enabling local levels, provincial governments, and development partners to cooperate and collaborate. Skill development programs such as the 'Earn While You Learn' concept-based National Apprenticeship Program, demand-based skill development programs, workplace-based training based on labor market demand, entrepreneurship promotion programs, skill development programs targeting the new digital sector AI, and skill development programs targeting the landless have been initiated from this year. Esteemed Chairperson, the government is also clear on the issue of foreign employment. Going abroad is not a problem in itself, but our clear stance is that no Nepali should be forced to go abroad for survival, and those who go abroad should be able to do so for transformative opportunities that yield high returns and bring positive changes in their lives. However, in the context of continuously increasing incidents of death, fraud, abandonment, and exploitation of Nepali citizens abroad, I also want to present the work done by the ministry to control such activities and rescue those in trouble. Details of citizens requiring rescue from Nepali embassies abroad are being sought, and rescue operations are being carried out through the Foreign Employment Board for those with labor permits and in coordination with the respective embassies for those without labor permits. Furthermore, work is underway to create an environment to prevent fraud and exploitation by amending the Foreign Employment Act, 2064, to be timely and developing a fully automated system. Similarly, to discourage fraudulent activities, as a promotional program, the Safe Migration Program is being operated by providing services at all 753 local levels and 102 district administration offices and area administration offices, offering counseling services to every person obtaining a passport. For those with all documents in order, arrangements have been made to provide labor permits within two hours by simplifying the process, and the process for re-issuing labor permits has been fully automated. Furthermore, the monitoring of the performance of licensed agencies has been made more effective. With the objective of making complaint management easier and more effective, an online portal, ujuri.dfe.gov.np, has been launched for submitting complaints, including those of victims of fraud, and immediate action is being taken on the complaints received. To take action against illegal agents and intermediaries who defraud, exploit, or force Nepali workers seeking foreign employment into forced labor, an app named 'Operation Illegal Agent Cleanup Towards Safer Migration' has been launched...

The Ministry has also initiated the process of taking action based on the investigation of the complaint. A complaint hearing center has been brought into operation at the ministry level to address grievances promptly, and arrangements have been made for the immediate resolution of complaints. In coordination with the Ministry of Home Affairs, District Administration Offices, and District Police Offices, efforts are underway to facilitate reconciliation, apprehend offenders, and expedite legal proceedings. Public awareness regarding foreign employment fraud has been enhanced through the effective implementation of pre-decision and pre-departure orientation training programs. The training content is also being prepared in digital format and disseminated through various media channels. Furthermore, in coordination with diplomatic missions related to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Foreign Employment Board, the management of the bodies of Nepali citizens residing abroad and other rescue and relief efforts are continuously ongoing. By maximizing the use of information technology, integrating and automating service delivery to create an environment where fraud is impossible, and establishing good governance throughout the entire chain of foreign employment through effective labor diplomacy, are also priorities of our Ministry.

Finally, the government has taken the issue raised by the honorable member seriously. We commit to moving forward by making this not just a ministry-level issue but a priority for the entire government and the state. As we conclude, I would like to state one thing. Until now, we have handed visas into the hands of our youth, but we have not been able to provide employment opportunities in our own country. We have been proud of the remittances sent by youth going abroad, but we have not questioned why they are forced to go abroad. The country's workforce has been leaving, villages have become empty, families have been separated, but our policies have continued on the same old path. That path will now change. Leaving the country is not the dream of our youth; it is the search for opportunity. If they find opportunities in Nepal, why would they leave their homeland? We are not giving speeches to stop youth from going abroad; rather, we are building a Nepal where the decision to go abroad or stay in Nepal is made by opportunity, not by compulsion. We will build a Nepal where the youth, looking back, can say their future is here. Thank you.

(14:00 hrs) ...will be given time to ask supplementary questions focusing on the topic.
Honorable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson,
(14:00 hrs) ...Through you, my supplementary question to the minister is as follows: It has been 139 days since the new government was formed, which promised to provide employment to all youth with a snap of the fingers during the election campaign. Why has this not happened? What is the total number of migrant workers who have gone to various countries for foreign employment but are stranded due to various reasons? Among them, how many are women migrant workers? Since the formation of this government, how many such stranded migrant workers have been repatriated to Nepal? When will the remaining stranded workers be brought back? In other words, when will the environment for legal work be created? How many youth have received new employment from the 753 local levels? Many policies and systems have been created; what are the concrete results that citizens will see in the next one year, honorable minister?

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Minister.
(15:01 hrs)
(14:01 hrs)
Honorable Minister of Youth, Labor and Employment, Mr. Ramji Yadav: Actually, for job creation in our country, the ministry is working on it. There is no policy or act in place. The National Employment Policy was formulated in 2071 BS, but no act has been advanced for its implementation. Now, we are revising the National Employment Policy and transforming it into the National Employment Act, and we are advancing employment policies and programs. Through these existing programs, we are implementing programs from the National Apprenticeship Program to skills-based employment. These programs have been launched and are about to be launched. Once they are implemented, I will provide a response on how much employment has been created and what has happened. Regarding the other matter, we are regularly processing the cases of youth residing abroad who are victims, who wish to be rescued, and who want to return to Nepal. It's not that we have brought back a certain number at once and will bring back a certain number; it's a regular process. We are providing relief and rescue to 2-4 individuals daily. Regarding compensation, if you talk about relief and compensation, while 12 crore was paid in the last nine months, we have paid 31 crore in compensation within three months. The rate of settlement of compensation claims has increased by 243%. This is the work done in three months, which we have also publicized as work done within 100 days. Therefore, we are trying to operate differently now, unlike in the past. In the coming days, we will definitely create an environment where youth who wish to go abroad do so not out of compulsion but for opportunity, to transform their lives and families, and to seek better salaries. We are creating such an environment. For that, we will definitely show some progress this year and I will publicize it again here. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: I now request the honorable minister to take his seat.
(15:04 hrs)

Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Gita Chaudhary, to present the proposal to send the Infectious Animal Disease Control Bill, 2083, to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-wise discussion.

Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Ms. Gita Chaudhary: Honorable Chairperson,
(14:04 hrs) ...Sir, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the proposal to send the Infectious Animal Disease Control Bill, 2083, to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-wise discussion before this respected assembly. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now present the proposal to send the Infectious Animal Disease Control Bill, 2083, to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-wise discussion for a decision. Honorable members in favor of this proposal will say "Yes" and honorable members against it will say "No".

Honorable members in favor of this proposal, say "Yes".
-"Yes"
Honorable members against this proposal, say "No".
"No" was not heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal to send the Infectious Animal Disease Control Bill, 2083, to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-wise discussion has been unanimously approved.

Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will convene on Wednesday, Bhadra 3, 2083 BS, at 1:15 PM. This meeting is hereby adjourned.
(Subsequently, this meeting was adjourned to reconvene on Wednesday, Bhadra 3, 2083 BS, at 1:15 PM.)
Adjourned: 15:06 hrs.

sections.summary_en: The meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of Honourable Chairperson Narayan Prasad Dahal. The proceedings began, and the Chairperson announced that names had been received to speak during Zero Hour.

sections.summary_en: Several members spoke during Zero Hour, raising issues such as the gas shortage affecting citizens, objectionable statements made by an MP, the impact of continuous rainfall and landslides, and the government's focus on propaganda over results. Concerns were also raised about the lack of alternatives for cooking and the need for government accountability.
